edits.find: Herpes makes monomorphic vesicles evolving into "punched-out" erosions with hemorrhagic crust and scalloped coalescing borders. Impetigo makes honey-colored crust — hemorrhagic ≠ honey. Diagnosis is clinical, confirmed with HSV PCR of vesicle fluid (Tzanck shows multinucleated giant cells, less sensitive). edits.find: Two findings settle this and both are on the examination rather than in the history. The patch carries overlying scale, which means an inflammatory or infectious process in the skin rather than a hair that is simply being pulled or shed; and the occipital and posterior auricular nodes are enlarged and tender, which is regional lymphadenopathy draining an infected scalp. Together they name tinea capitis — a dermatophyte that, unlike tinea of the body, invades the hair follicle and shaft, so the hair breaks and the patch expands centrifugally over weeks. The recent school change and the anxiety are the stem's deliberate offer of trichotillomania, and neither scale nor tender nodes belongs to that diagnosis.
